label: Mark 2:1
text: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.

label: Mark 2:2
text: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.

label: Mark 2:3
text: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.

label: Mark 2:4
text: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.

label: Mark 2:5
text:
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic,
“Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

label: Mark 2:6
text: But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

label: Mark 2:7
text: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

label: Mark 2:8
text:
Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them,
“Why do you reason these things in your hearts?

label: Mark 2:9
text: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’

label: Mark 2:10
text: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—

label: Mark 2:11
text: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”

label: Mark 2:12
text: He arose, and immediately took up the mat, and went out in front of them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”

label: Mark 2:13
text: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.

label: Mark 2:14
text:
As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him,
“Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.

label: Mark 2:15
text: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.

label: Mark 2:16
text: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”

label: Mark 2:17
text:
When Jesus heard it, he said to them,
“Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

label: Mark 2:18
text: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”

label: Mark 2:19
text:
Jesus said to them,
“Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.

label: Mark 2:20
text: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.

label: Mark 2:21
text: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.

label: Mark 2:22
text: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”

label: Mark 2:23
text: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.

label: Mark 2:24
text: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”

label: Mark 2:25
text:
He said to them,
“Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?

label: Mark 2:26
text: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”

variants.reading: ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ τοῦ ἱερέως ('when Abiatar was priest', without 'high')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ τοῦ ἱερέως in Δ (Codex Sangallensis) and itf - neither is a manuscript node of this graph.

variants.reading: the phrase 'when Abiatar was high priest' omitted
variants.note: The fetched article lists 'phrase is omitted by manuscripts D W 1009. 1546' with Old Latin and Old Syriac support; W (Codex Washingtonianus) is a manuscript node of this graph, D (Codex Bezae) is not. The main reading ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθαρ ἀρχιερέως ('when Abiatar was high priest') is carried by א A B K L and the Byzantine text.

label: Mark 2:27
text:
He said to them,
“The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

label: Mark 2:28
text: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

statement: Unable to come near Jesus for the crowd, the paralytic's carriers dug through the roof where he was and lowered the mat the paralytic lay on.
label: Roof dug open and the paralytic lowered

statement: Levi the son of Alphaeus sat at the tax office (telonion) and was called by Jesus to follow him.
label: Levi son of Alphaeus at the tax office

statement: David ate the showbread, which is lawful for priests alone, 'in the days of Abiathar the high priest'.
label: The showbread episode 'in the days of Abiathar the high priest'
Levi son of Alphaeus
aka: the tax collector of Mark 2:14; traditionally identified with Matthew the apostle

label: Abiathar
aka: son of Ahimelech; last high priest of Eli's house
dates: high priest under David; deposed by Solomon (1 Kings 2:27)

label: Capernaum (house construction: light roofs, stairs to the roof)
title: Capernaum
excerpt: and the roof would have been constructed of light wooden beams and thatch mixed with mud. This, along with the discovery of stairs to the roof, recalls the story of the Healing of the Paralytic from Mark 2:4

label: Matthew the Apostle (Levi son of Alphaeus)
title: Matthew the Apostle
excerpt: describe Jesus's calling of the tax collector Levi, the son of Alphaeus. They do not associate it with the name Matthew, but all three passages are remarkably similar.

label: Abiathar (Mark's naming versus Ahimelech)
title: Abiathar
excerpt: in reporting Jesus' words, the evangelist used the name Abiathar when we might expect to see Jesus mention his father Ahimelech

label: Showbread table depicted on the Arch of Titus relief
found: relief panel of Titus and Vespasian's triumphal procession, Arch of Titus, Rome

label: Showbread (Arch of Titus depiction)
title: Showbread
excerpt: The table is depicted on the Arch of Titus during the emperors Titus and Vespasian 's triumphal procession in 71 CE, which celebrated their defeat of Judea .
